evals.name: sky-blue-eli5
evals.prompt: my 7 year old keeps asking me why the sky is blue and i keep giving her a bad answer. can you make me something interactive i can actually sit down and go through with her?
evals.expected_output: One HTML file at eli5 level. Tactile, obvious cause-and-effect widgets, no equations, analogies flagged as analogies. Level inferred from 'my 7 year old' without being asked.
assertions: Produces exactly one self-contained HTML file that opens on its own with no server
Has at least 3 distinct interactive widgets, each tied to a different mechanism
Every slider has a live readout showing its current value with units
No control opens at its minimum, so the page is already showing something on load
Renders correctly in both light and dark mode
Has an explicit section naming its simplifications or where the model stops applying
At least one widget lets the reader push a parameter past where the model holds
Page renders with no JavaScript console errors
No fabricated numbers, citations, studies, or names
Written for a 7-year-old: no equations, concrete comparisons instead of numbers
Every analogy is flagged as an analogy and says where it breaks

evals.name: pid-derivative-kick-expert
evals.prompt: i've been tuning PID loops for 6 years and I still think the way textbooks present derivative kick is misleading. build me something that actually shows what happens on a setpoint step with D on error vs D on measurement, and where the standard 'just filter it' advice falls over
evals.expected_output: One HTML file at expert level. No definition of what PID is, no motivation. Side-by-side comparison of the two D formulations, and a widget exploring where filtering fails. Level inferred from stated experience and the specificity of the ask.
assertions: Produces exactly one self-contained HTML file that opens on its own with no server
Has at least 3 distinct interactive widgets, each tied to a different mechanism
Every slider has a live readout showing its current value with units
No control opens at its minimum, so the page is already showing something on load
Renders correctly in both light and dark mode
Has an explicit section naming its simplifications or where the model stops applying
At least one widget lets the reader push a parameter past where the model holds
Page renders with no JavaScript console errors
No fabricated numbers, citations, studies, or names
Written for a practitioner: does not define PID, setpoint, or what a derivative term is
Directly compares D-on-error against D-on-measurement on the same setpoint step
Shows a regime where derivative filtering stops rescuing the loop

evals.prompt: im in 2nd year cs and gradient descent still feels like magic to me. i get the calculus, i just dont have any feel for why the learning rate matters so much or why it diverges. something i can play with would help
evals.expected_output: One HTML file at college level. Real equations typeset with KaTeX (auto-detected by the build script), a learning-rate widget that sweeps across the divergence threshold, assumptions stated.
